title: Default Values Pattern
story: You're building a greeting app. Most users just want "Hello!" — but sometimes they want a personalized greeting with their name. You need both options without rewriting code.
why: Default values make functions flexible. Provide a sensible default for common use cases, but let callers override it when needed.
analogy: Default values are like a coffee shop's "usual" order — the barista knows what you want unless you specify otherwise.
expected_output:
Pizza with cheese
Pizza with pepperoni
try_it: Create a `draw_line` function that takes a length (Int) and a symbol (Str). Then make `draw_short_line()` that draws 10 dashes by default. Call both.
tips: Write the full-featured function first, then the shortcut version that calls it with defaults
Name the shortcut version clearly: `greet()` vs `greet_person(name)`
This pattern is called the 'facade pattern' — a simple face on a more complex function
common_mistakes: Duplicating logic in both functions — the shortcut should CALL the full version, not reimplement it
Trying to use `= default` syntax in parameters — XIOM doesn't support that; use the two-function pattern instead
Forgetting that the shortcut function still needs `()` even with no parameters
